key_insight: AI Gamestore uses a large, continuously growing catalog of human-designed games as a scalable, open-ended benchmark to measure machine general intelligence, avoiding saturation from static tasks and promoting broad, human-like competency evaluation.
problem_solved: Current AI benchmarks are narrow, static, and quickly gamed; this work addresses the need for a diverse, evolving, and human-relevant evaluation suite that tests generalization across many types of real human activities.
method: Aggregate and curate a large, diverse corpus of human-created games and interactive tasks with a standardized interface for agents.
Provide an evaluation infrastructure that runs games at scale, collects per-task performance and transfer/generalization metrics, and supports continuous addition of new games.
Define game-agnostic scoring and aggregate metrics (e.g., coverage, robustness, zero-shot transfer) plus leaderboards and automated pipelines to prevent overfitting to specific tasks.
impact: Enables practitioners to benchmark agents on broad, human-relevant skills and to track generalization and robustness as models evolve, reducing incentive to overfit to narrow datasets and promoting development of more generally capable systems.
visual_elements: System architecture diagram: game ingestion → standardized API → agent evaluation → metrics/leaderboard
Heatmap or radar chart showing agent competency across diverse game categories (puzzle, strategy, reflex, social)
Timeline/flow showing continuous addition of games and how scores evolve to illustrate open-ended evaluation
Scatter plot of per-game difficulty vs. agent performance highlighting generalization and transfer failures
paper_title: AI Gamestore: Scalable, Open-Ended Evaluation of Machine General Intelligence with Human Games
paper_authors: Lance Ying, Ryan Truong, Prafull Sharma, Kaiya Ivy Zhao, Nathan Cloos
